title: The race for more keeps you busy.
subtitle: Competing in increase distracts from what matters
then: Ibn Kathir says people are {trap}preoccupied by love of the world{/trap}, its delights and adornments. The Prophet ﷺ recited this surah and said: the son of Adam says my wealth, my wealth, yet he only keeps {reward}what he ate, what he wore out, and what he gave in charity{/reward}.
now: Your neighbour gets a new car, so yours suddenly feels old. A colleague posts a holiday and you start pricing flights. {trap}More than them{/trap} becomes the goal without you deciding it. The verse names the race you did not sign up for.
old: I am not competing with anyone. I just want a good life.
new: The race for more quietly takes my attention. I keep only what I use or give.
try: Mute or unfollow one account today that makes you want things you do not need.

title: Until the day you are carried to the graveyard.
subtitle: The race ends at the cemetery

row.title: at the grave
sub: greed and hope outlive the body

then: Ibn Kathir says this distraction delays you {trap}until death comes and you become an inhabitant of the graves{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ said three follow the dead: family, wealth and deeds. {reward}Two return. Only the deeds remain.{/reward}
now: You have stood at a burial. The family walks back to the cars. The money stays in the bank account. {reward}Only what the person did goes down with them.{/reward} One day you will be the one they walk away from.
old: I will slow down and focus on Allah once I have enough.
new: The race does not stop on its own. It stops at the grave, so I step out of it now.
try: Visit a graveyard this week, or think of someone buried, and make dua for them.

title: No. You are going to find out.
subtitle: The first warning
then: Al-Hasan Al-Basri called this {trap}a threat after a threat{/trap}. Ad-Dahhak said the first one is addressed to {idea}those who disbelieve{/idea}, and the next to the believers.
now: Someone you trust tells you, gently but firmly: no, this is not right, you will see. You brush it off. Later you wish you had listened. {idea}This is Allah saying it to you{/idea}, with the time still left to listen.
old: I am sure the race for more is worth it.
new: Allah says no. I would rather believe Him now than find out later.
try: Ask yourself honestly: what am I chasing that Allah would say no to? Write one answer.

title: Then again, no. You are going to find out.
subtitle: The warning repeated, for believers too
then: Ad-Dahhak said this second warning means {idea}O you believers{/idea}. Repeating it makes clear that {trap}the race for more catches believers as well{/trap}, not only those who deny.
now: You pray, you fast, you give. And still the shopping cart, the promotion, the bigger house pull on you every day. {idea}The second warning is addressed to people like you.{/idea} Faith does not make you immune to the race.
old: I am religious, so this surah is not really about me.
new: The warning repeats for believers. My faith does not protect me from wanting more.
try: Look at your last five purchases. Ask which ones were for need and which for keeping up.

title: If you knew for certain, you would stop racing.
subtitle: Sure knowledge changes behaviour
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}if you knew with true knowledge{/idea}, you would not be {trap}diverted by rivalry for wealth{/trap} away from the Hereafter until you reached the graves. The verse leaves the end of the sentence open.
now: You know smoking harms you, but you know it like a fact on a packet. Then a friend gets the diagnosis and you know it differently. {idea}Certainty changes what your hands do.{/idea} This verse asks for that kind of knowing about the Hereafter.
old: I already know about the Hereafter. I have heard it many times.
new: Hearing is not certainty. If I truly knew, my habits would already be different.
try: Spend five minutes today reflecting on death and what follows, until it feels real, not just known.

title: You will see the Fire.
subtitle: What the warning was about
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}the explanation of the previous threat{/idea}: you shall come to know. The narrations say it is so fearsome that {trap}even the angels and Prophets would fall to their knees{/trap} at its sight.
now: Some things you only understand when you see them: a flood on the news, a burned house down the street. The verse says one day {trap}you will see this with your own eyes{/trap}. Let the sight you have not seen yet guide what you chase today.
old: The Fire is something far away and abstract.
new: It is a sight I will see. That makes my priorities today urgent.
try: Ask Allah three times today: O Allah, save me from the Fire.

title: Then you will see it with the eye of certainty.
subtitle: From knowing to seeing
then: Verse 5 spoke of {idea}knowledge of certainty{/idea}. Now comes {trap}the eye of certainty{/trap}: seeing it directly. Ibn Kathir says Allah threatens them with this sight, which is what the people of the Fire will see.
now: There is knowing a road is icy, and there is seeing your car slide. The first lets you slow down. The second just happens to you. {idea}The surah begs you to take the first kind of certainty{/idea}, while it can still change your driving.
old: I will believe it fully when I see it.
new: When I see it, certainty will be useless. I want it now, while it can change me.
try: Pick one habit you would drop if you saw the Hereafter today. Drop it for one day.

title: You will be asked about every comfort you enjoyed.
subtitle: Dates, cold water, health, free time

row.title: hungry
sub: the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Umar

then: The Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr and Umar went out hungry and were fed by an Ansari man. He ﷺ said: {idea}you will be asked about this{/idea}. He also said {trap}two favours most people are cheated in: health and free time{/trap}.
now: The cold water from the fridge. The pain-free morning. The Sunday afternoon with nothing to do. You do not think of these as luxuries. {reward}They are the delights you will be asked about{/reward}: did you thank Allah for them?
old: I live a normal life. I do not have any luxuries to answer for.
new: Health, food and free time are the delights. Gratitude is how I answer for them.
try: At your next meal, pause before eating and thank Allah for three specific things on the plate.
